steps.explanationAfterStep: As N₂ leaves, a ring C–C bond moves to the CH₂, which becomes part of the ring: six-membered becomes seven-membered. The OH lone pair makes C=O at the same time. This is a semipinacol rearrangement: as in the pinacol rearrangement, a group moves towards the leaving group and a C=O forms where it left.
Water takes the proton: cycloheptanone, one carbon larger than the starting ring.

title: Tiffeneau–Demjanov ring expansion
subtitle: A diazonium ion loses N₂ as a ring bond moves: cyclohexane to cycloheptanone
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 36

reactants.caption: the diazonium ion from 1-(aminomethyl)cyclohexan-1-ol and nitrous acid + water
hintTiers: N₂ is the best leaving group there is, but losing it here would leave a primary cation. Which bond on the carbinol carbon can move to the CH₂ as N₂ leaves?
Three arrows: the C–N bond breaks onto nitrogen, a ring C–C bond moves from the carbinol carbon to the CH₂, and the OH lone pair makes C=O.
C–N bond → a lone pair on nitrogen (N₂ leaves); ring C–C bond of the carbinol carbon → new bond from that ring carbon to the CH₂; OH oxygen lone pair → C=O π bond.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Nitrogen leaves, and the ring grows. Draw it as one step.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The oxygen can displace N₂ to give an epoxide, a known side product. The main reaction is the ring expansion, which makes a C=O bond.
Water could displace N₂ to give a diol, but the ring bond next door is already lined up to move: the ring expansion wins.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right that N₂ leaves, but on its own that would leave a primary carbocation. The ring C–C bond moves as N₂ goes, and the OH lone pair makes C=O.

protonated-ketone.caption: protonated cycloheptanone + N₂ + water
hintTiers: The carbonyl oxygen still carries a proton. Which base is present?
Water takes the proton; the O–H pair stays on the carbonyl oxygen. Two arrows.
Water oxygen lone pair → new bond to the drawn H; O–H bond → a lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Chloride is far too weak a base to take this proton. Water does it.

mechanismSummary: 1-(Aminomethyl)cyclohexan-1-ol is diazotised by nitrous acid (as aniline is; see Nucleophilic aromatic substitution), and the reaction starts here from the diazonium ion. N₂ leaves as a ring C–C bond moves to the CH₂ and the OH lone pair makes C=O: the ring grows by one carbon. Loss of a proton gives cycloheptanone. The first carbocation would be primary, so the shift and the loss of N₂ are drawn together.
